thread:
acme-admin: Hey team — we just did a bulk SCIM removal for ~25 contractors (`engineering-contractors` group) and they were removed from Okta but are still showing as active in our app. Can you help? This is ACME-5689.

acme-admin: Quick repro: remove user via Okta -> SCIM PATCH membership change -> Okta shows 204, Redwood SCIM logs show patch accepted, but user still has `contractor` role via group mapping.

acme-admin: Example user: alice+contractor@acme.com; Okta user id `00u1abcdXYZ`; SCIM payload we saw: 
```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {"op": "Remove", "path": "members[value eq \"00u1abcdXYZ\"]"}
  ]
}
```

emma cs: ack — pulling logs now. Do we have the SCIM webhook delivery id or request id?

acme-admin: webhook id `wh_20260315_8771` and scim-request `req-7f9b2`.

raj eng: I see the incoming PATCH handled at 2026-03-15T14:22:11Z and we returned 204. But the role removal job that translates group->role is async. There's an event processor lag in the group-sync queue.

raj eng: logs snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:22:11Z] scim: PATCH /v2/Groups/00g9xyz - req=req-7f9b2 - op=Remove members[value eq "00u1abcdXYZ"] -> 204
[2026-03-15T14:22:11Z] group-sync: enqueued job group:00g9xyz version:42 -> ok
[2026-03-15T14:22:11Z] group-sync-worker: picked job group:00g9xyz v:42
[2026-03-15T14:22:12Z] group-sync-worker: reconcile start for group:00g9xyz\n[2026-03-15T14:22:12Z] group-sync-worker: fetch members from Okta -> returns 24
[2026-03-15T14:22:12Z] group-sync-worker: update roles for 0 users (skip)
```

lena infra: that "returns 24" is suspicious — should be 24 after removal if original was 49, but acme said they removed 25. Could be that Okta returned cached membership or there was a nested-group reference. Do we support nested groups in their Okta setup?

acme-admin: yes — engineering-contractors is a group that contains `external-contractors` as nested group. We removed individual members but didn't touch the nested group.

sam security: nested groups are a known edge case — our group->role mapper only evaluates direct group membership in the current release. If a nested group still contains those users, the patch that removes direct member entries won't remove role because the resolver later sees them as members via nested group.

emma cs: so the net effect is: Okta removed direct membership but the nested group still gave them access. How did they end up in nested group? acme-admin: those users were also added to `external-contractors` by an Okta automation earlier.

raj eng: two problems then: 1) we returned 204 for the PATCH and enqueued reconcile job, but reconcile logic only looked at direct members; 2) we don't surface nested-group membership in the SCIM logs so CS couldn't tell.

emma cs: immediate ask from ACME: we need those 25 users' product access revoked now. Can we run a one-off reconciliation that expands nested groups?

lena infra: yes — we have an admin endpoint to force-run a full group resolution for a group id: `POST /internal/admin/groups/00g9xyz/reconcile?expand_nested=true`. I can run if we get explicit permission from ACME.

acme-admin: do it please, but only for `engineering-contractors` and please confirm which users will be affected before you change anything.

lena infra: on it — fetching candidate diff now.

okta-sync-bot: Okta webhook event replay available -> replay id `replay-20260315-01`

lena infra: diff preview: will remove `alice+contractor@acme.com`, `bob.contractor@acme.com`, and 23 others from role `contractor` and revoke token sessions for 17 of them. Preview attached.

acme-admin: confirm, please revoke sessions as well.

emma cs: tagging @sam security — we should also rotate any API keys those contractors might have. Are contractors allowed to create API keys?

sam security: not by policy, but some had keys prior to the change. We'll invalidate any active API keys tied to those user ids during the reconciliation run. Also will log the action for audit.

raj eng: action plan (short-term):
- lena to run reconcile with expand_nested=true after CS confirmation (manual safe mode)
- raj to add a migration to double-check nested membership during role reconciliation (patch will be low risk)
- sam to revoke sessions and invalidate API keys for affected users
- emma to inform ACME and coordinate maintenance window (should be < 5m)

acme-admin: agreed. Please keep me updated in this thread.

lena infra: executing in 2m — going to run in dry-run first then live.

lena infra: dry-run output: 25 users to unassign role `contractor`. No conflicts. Would you like me to proceed?

acme-admin: proceed.

lena infra: running live now...

oncall-bot: Incident transient-notice: scheduled admin action initiated by lena at 2026-03-15T14:34:05Z. Tracking ID inc-ACME-20260315-01.

lena infra: completed — 25 users unassigned, 17 sessions revoked, 4 API keys invalidated. Audit log: `audit-20260315-ACME-5689`.

acme-admin: confirmed — users no longer have access. Thanks everyone. Big ask: can we get a permanent fix so nested groups are considered automatically?

raj eng: on it. I'll open PR to update the group-sync worker to resolve nested groups and make group->role mapping idempotent across both direct and transitive membership. Will include regression test and an optional feature flag so we can rollout gradually.

sam security: also recommending we add a safety check in SCIM handling: if Okta sends both a remove op and there's evidence of nested membership, surface a warning to CS and include the nested membership list in the webhook payload we persist.

emma cs: I'll draft the customer-facing postmortem and an action summary: what happened, immediate mitigation, and long-term roadmap. Will send to ACME once PR lands.

raj eng: estimate for code fix + tests + rollout: 2 sprints if no surprises. Quick mitigation (add nested expansion flag to reconcile endpoint) is done.

acme-admin: appreciated. One follow-up: can we get a list of other customers using nested groups so we can proactively check?

emma cs: yes — I'll run a tenant-scan for group configs and flag any tenants with nested groups and open tickets to proactively offer reconciliation.

acme-admin: thanks, closing on our side.

emma cs: closing thread after PR and tenant-scan follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
